category: PSpice digital simulation: U primitives, stimulus generators, timing and I/O models, interfaces and constraint checkers
description: The digital side of PSpice A/D: the U device syntax, every primitive family (gates, tristate gates, transfer gates, flip-flops and latches, pull resistors, delay lines, PLDs, ROM/RAM, ADC/DAC, pin-to-pin delay and constraint checkers), the STIM/FSTIM stimulus devices and their command language, the timing-model parameter naming scheme, the UIO I/O model, analog/digital interface subcircuits and power nodes, and the worst-case timing and hazard reporting machinery.

tools.name: U (digital primitive, general form)
tools.description: Declaration of any digital primitive: type with its parenthesised parameters (e.g. number of inputs), the digital power and ground nodes used by interface subcircuits, the I/O nodes in the order the primitive defines, a timing model and an I/O model, plus optional MNTYMXDLY and IO_LEVEL selectors. Library parts such as 74LS00 are subcircuits built from these primitives.
tools.usage: U<name> <primitive type> [(<parameter value>*)] <digital power node> <digital ground node> <node>* <timing model name> <I/O model name> [MNTYMXDLY=<0..4>] [IO_LEVEL=<0..4>]

parameters.name: <primitive type>
parameters.description: NAND, JKFF, STIM, PLAND, ROM, ADC, CONSTRAINT ...

parameters.name: <timing model name>
parameters.description: .MODEL of the primitive-specific type (UGATE, UEFF, UDLY ...).

parameters.name: <I/O model name>
parameters.description: .MODEL of type UIO (IO_STD, IO_LS, IO_HC ...).

parameters.name: MNTYMXDLY
parameters.description: 0 use .OPTIONS DIGMNTYMX, 1 min, 2 typ, 3 max, 4 worst-case.

parameters.name: IO_LEVEL
parameters.description: 0 use .OPTIONS DIGIOLVL, 1-4 select AtoDn/DtoAn interface pair.

tools.example:
U1 NAND(2) $G_DPWR $G_DGND 1 2 10 D0_GATE IO_DFT
U2 JKFF(1) $G_DPWR $G_DGND 3 5 200 3 3 10 2 D_293ASTD IO_STD
U3 INV $G_DPWR $G_DGND IN OUT D_INV IO_INV MNTYMXDLY=3 IO_LEVEL=2
tools.notes: Nodes with both analog and digital connections get interface subcircuits inserted automatically. PULLUP, PULLDN and PINDLY have no timing model.

tools.name: Standard gates: BUF, INV, AND, NAND, OR, NOR, XOR, NXOR
tools.description: Simple logic gates with one output. AND/NAND/OR/NOR take (<no. of inputs>); BUF, INV, XOR and NXOR have fixed pin counts. X propagates only when it could change the output (1 AND X = X, 0 AND X = 0). Timing comes from a UGATE model with TPLH/TPHL min/typ/max delays.
tools.usage:
U<name> AND|NAND|OR|NOR(<no. of inputs>) <pwr> <gnd> <in>* <out> <UGATE model> <UIO model>
U<name> BUF|INV <pwr> <gnd> <in> <out> <UGATE model> <UIO model>
U<name> XOR|NXOR <pwr> <gnd> <in1> <in2> <out> <UGATE model> <UIO model>

parameters.name: (<no. of inputs>)
parameters.description: Input count for AND/NAND/OR/NOR.

tools.example:
U1 AND(2) $G_DPWR $G_DGND IN1 IN2 OUT T_AND2 IO_STD
U2 INV $G_DPWR $G_DGND 3 5 T_INV IO_STD
.MODEL T_AND2 UGATE(TPLHMN=5ns TPLHTY=10ns TPLHMX=15ns TPHLMN=5ns TPHLTY=10ns TPHLMX=15ns)
tools.notes: Pulses shorter than the propagation delay are swallowed (suppressed-glitch hazard); a DLYLINE passes any width.

tools.name: Gate arrays: BUFA, INVA, ANDA, NANDA, ORA, NORA, XORA, NXORA
tools.description: Several identical gates in one primitive, matching multi-gate packages. ANDA/NANDA/ORA/NORA take (<no. of inputs>,<no. of gates>); BUFA/INVA/XORA/NXORA take (<no. of gates>). Node order: all inputs of gate 1, all inputs of gate 2, ..., then all outputs in gate order.
tools.usage:
U<name> ANDA|NANDA|ORA|NORA(<no. of inputs>,<no. of gates>) <pwr> <gnd> <in>* <out>* <UGATE model> <UIO model>
U<name> BUFA|INVA|XORA|NXORA(<no. of gates>) <pwr> <gnd> <in>* <out>* <UGATE model> <UIO model>

parameters.name: (<no. of inputs>,<no. of gates>)
parameters.description: Per-gate inputs and number of gates.

tools.example: U13 NANDA(2,4) $G_DPWR $G_DGND INA0 INA1 INB0 INB1 INC0 INC1 IND0 IND1 OUTA OUTB OUTC OUTD T_NANDA IO_STD
tools.notes: All gates share one timing model; per-gate variation is not possible in one array.

tools.name: Tristate gates: BUF3, INV3, AND3, NAND3, OR3, NOR3, XOR3, NXOR3 (and *3A arrays)
tools.description: Gates with an enable input: when enable is 0 the output strength is Z and its level X. Timing model type UTGATE adds enable-related delays TPZH/TPZL/TPHZ/TPLZ (min/typ/max) to the normal TPLH/TPHL. Array forms (BUF3A, NAND3A ...) share one enable placed after all inputs and before all outputs.
tools.usage:
U<name> AND3|NAND3|OR3|NOR3(<no. of inputs>) <pwr> <gnd> <in>* <enable> <out> <UTGATE model> <UIO model>
U<name> BUF3|INV3 <pwr> <gnd> <in> <enable> <out> <UTGATE model> <UIO model>
U<name> NAND3A(<no. of inputs>,<no. of gates>) <pwr> <gnd> <in>* <enable> <out>* <UTGATE model> <UIO model>

parameters.name: TPZHxx / TPZLxx
parameters.description: Enable-to-output (Z to H/L) delays.

parameters.name: TPHZxx / TPLZxx
parameters.description: Disable (H/L to Z) delays.

tools.example:
U5 AND3(2) $G_DPWR $G_DGND IN0 IN1 ENABLE OUT T_TRIAND2 IO_STD
.MODEL T_TRIAND2 UTGATE(TPLHMN=15ns TPLHTY=20ns TPLHMX=25ns TPZHMN=10ns TPZHTY=15ns TPZHMX=20ns)
tools.notes: A tristate output on a net with INLD/OUTLD capacitance > 0 makes that net a charge-storage net that remembers its last level for TSTOREMN.

tools.name: NBTG / PBTG (bidirectional transfer gates)
tools.description: N- and P-channel bidirectional transfer (pass) gates: a gate node controls a channel between two nodes in either direction, modelled with a UBTG timing model. When the gate connects to an analog net PSpice inserts an AtoD interface; using the '_D' DtoA variants (IO_LEVEL 3/4) avoids converting large parts of the circuit to analog.
tools.usage: U<name> NBTG|PBTG <pwr> <gnd> <gate node> <channel node 1> <channel node 2> <UBTG model> <UIO model> [MNTYMXDLY=..] [IO_LEVEL=..]

parameters.name: <channel node 1/2>
parameters.description: The two switched terminals; signals pass both ways.

tools.example:
U4 NBTG $G_DPWR $G_DGND GATE SD1 SD2 BTG1 IO_BTG
.MODEL BTG1 UBTG
.model io_nbtg uio (drvh=200 drvl=200 inld=10pf outld=15pf digpower="DIGIFPWR" TstoreMN=10us inR=10MEG drvZ=5MEG)
tools.notes: Used to build CMOS analogue switches (4066) and bus switches in the digital domain.

tools.name: DFF / JKFF (edge-triggered flip-flops)
tools.description: Arrays of edge-triggered flip-flops sharing presetbar, clearbar and clock (JKFF clocks on the falling edge of clockbar; DFF on the rising clock edge), followed by n data (or J and K) inputs, n Q and n Qbar outputs. Timing model type UEFF carries setup, hold, propagation and minimum-width parameters and drives timing-violation messages.
tools.usage:
U<name> DFF(<n>) <pwr> <gnd> <presetbar> <clearbar> <clock> <d1>..<dn> <q1>..<qn> <qbar1>..<qbarn> <UEFF model> <UIO model>
U<name> JKFF(<n>) <pwr> <gnd> <presetbar> <clearbar> <clockbar> <j1>..<jn> <k1>..<kn> <q1>..<qn> <qbar1>..<qbarn> <UEFF model> <UIO model>

parameters.name: (<n>)
parameters.description: Number of flip-flops sharing the control pins.

tools.example:
U2 DFF(2) $G_DPWR $G_DGND PREBAR CLRBAR CLK D0 D1 Q0 Q1 QBAR0 QBAR1 T_DFF IO_STD
U5 JKFF(1) $G_DPWR $G_DGND PREBAR CLRBAR CLKBAR J K Q QBAR T_JKFF IO_STD
tools.notes: Initial state is X unless .OPTIONS DIGINITSTATE sets 0 or 1 or a reset is applied. Tie unused preset/clear to a logic-1 node ($D_HI) rather than leaving them open.

tools.name: DFFDE / JKFFDE (dual-edge flip-flops)
tools.description: Flip-flops that can be triggered on the positive and/or negative clock edge, selected dynamically through two extra enable nodes (positive-edge enable, negative-edge enable) placed after the clock. Same UEFF timing model as DFF/JKFF; used for DDR-style and dual-edge counters.
tools.usage: U<name> DFFDE(<n>) <pwr> <gnd> <presetbar> <clrbar> <clock> <pos-edge enable> <neg-edge enable> <d>* <q>* <qbar>* <UEFF model> <UIO model>

parameters.name: <pos-edge enable> / <neg-edge enable>
parameters.description: Logic-1 enables triggering on that edge; common to all flip-flops in the array.

tools.example: U7 DFFDE(1) $G_DPWR $G_DGND $D_HI $D_HI CLK $D_HI $D_HI D Q QBAR T_DFF IO_STD

tools.name: SRFF / DLTCH (gated flip-flop and latch)
tools.description: Level-sensitive (gated) storage elements: SRFF is a gated set/reset flip-flop and DLTCH a transparent D latch, both arrays with shared presetbar, clearbar and gate nodes. Their timing model type is UGFF with gate-related delays (TPGQ), setup/hold to the gate edge and minimum gate width.
tools.usage:
U<name> SRFF(<n>) <pwr> <gnd> <presetbar> <clearbar> <gate> <s1>..<sn> <r1>..<rn> <q>* <qbar>* <UGFF model> <UIO model>
U<name> DLTCH(<n>) <pwr> <gnd> <presetbar> <clearbar> <gate> <d1>..<dn> <q>* <qbar>* <UGFF model> <UIO model>

parameters.name: <gate>
parameters.description: While high the latch is transparent; it holds on the falling edge.

tools.example:
U9 DLTCH(4) $G_DPWR $G_DGND $D_HI $D_HI LE D0 D1 D2 D3 Q0 Q1 Q2 Q3 QB0 QB1 QB2 QB3 T_LATCH IO_STD
.MODEL T_LATCH UGFF(TPDQLHTY=15ns TPDQHLTY=15ns TPGQLHTY=12ns TPGQHLTY=12ns TSUDGTY=5ns THDGTY=3ns)

tools.name: PULLUP / PULLDN (pull resistor arrays)
tools.description: Arrays of digital pull-up or pull-down 'resistors' that drive their nodes weakly to 1 or 0 so that open-collector/tristate busses resolve. They have an I/O model only (no timing model); the drive strength comes from the I/O model's DRVH/DRVL.
tools.usage: U<name> PULLUP|PULLDN(<number of resistors>) <pwr> <gnd> <node>* <UIO model>

parameters.name: (<number of resistors>)
parameters.description: Number of nodes pulled.

tools.example:
U5 PULLUP(4) $G_DPWR $G_DGND BUS0 BUS1 BUS2 BUS3 R1K
U2 PULLDN(1) $G_DPWR $G_DGND 15 R500
tools.notes: dig_io.lib provides R1K/R500-style I/O models with appropriately weak DRVH/DRVL; the DIGOVRDRV ratio decides when a real driver overrides the pull.

tools.name: DLYLINE (delay line)
tools.description: Pure digital delay element whose output follows the input after the UDLY model delay (DLYMN/DLYTY/DLYMX). Unlike gates it propagates pulses of any width, so it is the right primitive for modelling cable, trace or explicit delay-line parts.
tools.usage: U<name> DLYLINE <pwr> <gnd> <input node> <output node> <UDLY model> <UIO model> [MNTYMXDLY=..] [IO_LEVEL=..]

parameters.name: DLYMN / DLYTY / DLYMX
parameters.description: Minimum, typical and maximum delay in the UDLY model.

tools.example:
U5 DLYLINE $G_DPWR $G_DGND IN OUT DLY20NS IO_STD
.MODEL DLY20NS UDLY(DLYMN=20ns DLYTY=20ns DLYMX=20ns)

tools.name: PLD primitives: PLAND, PLOR, PLXOR, PLNAND, PLNOR, PLNXOR and *C (true/complement) forms
tools.description: Programmable logic arrays: inputs form columns, outputs rows, each row driven by one gate of the array type; the *C variants provide both true and complement of every input. The program comes from a JEDEC file (FILE=, normally through a TEXT parameter JEDEC_FILE) or in-line DATA=<radix>$...$. Timing model type UPLD. Library PAL/GAL parts wrap these so you only supply the JEDEC file name.
tools.usage: U<name> <pld type>(<no. of inputs>,<no. of outputs>) <pwr> <gnd> <input node>* <output node>* <UPLD model> <UIO model> [FILE=<file name text value>] [DATA=<radix flag>$<program data>$] [MNTYMXDLY=..] [IO_LEVEL=..]

parameters.name: FILE
parameters.description: JEDEC file name (text constant or |text expression|).

parameters.name: DATA
parameters.description: B$ / O$ / X$ radix flag followed by fuse data terminated by $.

tools.example:
UDECODE PLANDC(3, 8) $G_DPWR $G_DGND IN1 IN2 IN3 OUT0 OUT1 OUT2 OUT3 OUT4 OUT5 OUT6 OUT7 PLD_MDL IO_STD
+ DATA=B$ 01 01 01  01 01 10  01 10 01  01 10 10  10 01 01  10 01 10  10 10 01  10 10 10 $
X1 I1 I2 I3 O1 PAL14H4 TEXT: JEDEC_FILE="myprog.jed"

tools.name: ROM (read-only memory)
tools.description: Digital ROM with an enable, address inputs (msb first) and data outputs, programmed from an Intel-Hex file (FILE=) or in-line DATA. Timing model type UROM gives access and enable delays. The reference example is a 4x4-bit multiplier built as an 8-address-bit, 8-output ROM.
tools.usage: U<name> ROM(<no. of address pins>,<no. of output pins>) <pwr> <gnd> <enable node> <address msb>..<address lsb> <output msb>..<output lsb> <UROM model> <UIO model> [FILE=<hex file>] [DATA=<radix flag>$<data>$]

parameters.name: FILE
parameters.description: Intel Hex format program file.

parameters.name: DATA
parameters.description: In-line contents, msb first.

tools.example: UMULTIPLY ROM(8, 8) $G_DPWR $G_DGND EN A7 A6 A5 A4 A3 A2 A1 A0 D7 D6 D5 D4 D3 D2 D1 D0 ROM_MDL IO_STD FILE="mult.hex"

tools.name: RAM (random-access memory)
tools.description: Digital RAM with read-enable and write-enable, address pins, separate write-data and read-data busses, optionally initialised from an Intel-Hex file or in-line DATA. Timing model type URAM specifies read access, write pulse and setup/hold parameters.
tools.usage: U<name> RAM(<no. of address bits>,<no. of output bits>) <pwr> <gnd> <read enable> <write enable> <address msb>..<lsb> <write-data msb>..<lsb> <read-data msb>..<lsb> <URAM model> <UIO model> [FILE=<hex file>] [DATA=<radix flag>$<init data>$]

parameters.name: FILE
parameters.description: Intel Hex initialisation file; overrides DATA.

tools.example: UMEM RAM(4, 8) $G_DPWR $G_DGND RE WE A3 A2 A1 A0 WD7 WD6 WD5 WD4 WD3 WD2 WD1 WD0 RD7 RD6 RD5 RD4 RD3 RD2 RD1 RD0 RAM_MDL IO_STD

tools.name: ADC (multi-bit analog-to-digital converter)
tools.description: Behavioural n-bit ADC primitive: analog input, reference and ground nodes, a convert strobe, status and over-range outputs and n digital outputs. Timing model UADC gives conversion delays (TPCSMN.. from convert edge to status/data). The analog input pins are true analog nodes, so no interface subcircuit is needed.
tools.usage: U<name> ADC(<number of bits>) <pwr> <gnd> <in node> <ref node> <gnd node> <convert node> <status node> <over-range node> <output msb>..<output lsb> <UADC model> <UIO model>

parameters.name: <ref node>
parameters.description: Full-scale reference voltage input.

parameters.name: <status node>
parameters.description: Busy flag during conversion.

tools.example:
U5 ADC(4) $G_DPWR $G_DGND Sig Ref 0 Conv Stat OvrRng Out3 Out2 Out1 Out0 ADCModel IO_STD
.MODEL ADCModel UADC(TPCSMN=10ns TPCSTY=20ns TPCSMX=30ns)
tools.notes: Capture parts ADC8break/ADC10break etc. wrap this primitive.

tools.name: DAC (multi-bit digital-to-analog converter)
tools.description: Behavioural n-bit DAC: a zero-impedance voltage source from out to gnd whose value is ref * binary input / 2^n, with switching times from the UDAC model (TSWMN/TSWTY/TSWMX, default 10 ns). Data inputs are digital nodes; out/ref/gnd are analog.
tools.usage: U<name> DAC(<number of bits>) <pwr> <gnd> <out node> <ref node> <gnd node> <input msb>..<input lsb> <UDAC model> <UIO model>

parameters.name: TSWMN / TSWTY / TSWMX
parameters.description: Data change to analog output stable.

tools.example:
U7 DAC(4) $G_DPWR $G_DGND Sig Ref 0 In3 In2 In1 In0 DACModel IO_STD
.MODEL DACModel UDAC(TSWMN=10ns TSWTY=15ns TSWMX=20ns)
tools.notes: Capture parts DAC8break etc. Use an R-C on the output to model settling if needed.

tools.name: PINDLY (pin-to-pin delay primitive)
tools.description: Models path-dependent delays of a complete device: inputs, optional enable and reference nodes, outputs, with BOOLEAN: assignments, PINDLY: delay assignments per output (using transition functions such as CHANGED, TRN_LH, DELAY(min,typ,max)), TRISTATE: sections and embedded SETUP_HOLD/WIDTH/FREQ/GENERAL constraints. It is how library ICs get datasheet-accurate pin-to-pin timing on top of functional primitives.
tools.usage:
U<name> PINDLY(<no. of paths>,<no. of enables>,<no. of refs>) <pwr> <gnd> <input>* [<enable>*] [<reference>*] <output>* <UIO model> [MNTYMXDLY=..] [IO_LEVEL=..]
+ [BOOLEAN: <var>={<expr>} ...]
+ PINDLY: <output>={<delay expression>} ...
+ [TRISTATE: ENABLE LO|HI <enable node> <delay assignment>*]
+ [SETUP_HOLD: ...] [WIDTH: ...] [FREQ: ...] [GENERAL: ...]

parameters.name: PINDLY:
parameters.description: Per-output delay expressions, e.g. CASE(TRN_LH & CHANGED(IN1,0), DELAY(5ns,10ns,15ns), DELAY(...)).

parameters.name: TRISTATE:
parameters.description: Delays applied when the named enable is at the stated level.

tools.notes: Unlike CONSTRAINT, constraints inside PINDLY can propagate hazards to the outputs (AFFECTS clauses). Most users meet PINDLY only when reading library subcircuits.

tools.name: CONSTRAINT (timing constraint checker)
tools.description: Primitive that only reports timing violations and never changes logic states or delays. It takes the device's input nodes and one or more constraint sections: SETUP_HOLD, WIDTH, FREQ and GENERAL, optionally with BOOLEAN helper variables. Violations go to the .out file (and Probe) as SETUP, HOLD, RELEASE, WIDTH, FREQUENCY or GENERAL messages, subject to DIGERRDEFAULT/DIGERRLIMIT.
tools.usage: U<name> CONSTRAINT(<no. of inputs>) <pwr> <gnd> <input node>* <UIO model> [IO_LEVEL=..] [BOOLEAN: <assignment>*] [SETUP_HOLD: ...] [WIDTH: ...] [FREQ: ...] [GENERAL: ...]

parameters.name: BOOLEAN:
parameters.description: <var> = { <boolean expression> } definitions usable in WHEN clauses.

parameters.name: ERRORLIMIT
parameters.description: Per-section message cap overriding DIGERRDEFAULT.

parameters.name: MESSAGE
parameters.description: Extra text appended to the violation report.

tools.example:
UCHK CONSTRAINT(3) $G_DPWR $G_DGND CLK D CLRBAR IO_STD
+ SETUP_HOLD: CLOCK LH=CLK DATA(1)=D SETUPTIME=20ns HOLDTIME=5ns WHEN {CLRBAR=='1'}
+ WIDTH: NODE=CLK MIN_LOW=15ns MIN_HIGH=15ns
+ FREQ: NODE=CLK MAXFREQ=25MEG
tools.notes: The GENERAL section evaluates an arbitrary Boolean over the inputs and reports when it becomes true. .EXTERNAL nets turn hazards reaching them into PERSISTENT HAZARD reports.

tools.name: SETUP_HOLD: constraint section
tools.description: Setup/hold/release checker inside CONSTRAINT or PINDLY: names the CLOCK node with its asserting edge (LH or HL), the DATA nodes, and SETUPTIME, HOLDTIME and RELEASETIME (each optionally split into _LO/_HI or _LH/_HL variants for level- or edge-dependent datasheet values). A WHEN expression gates the check, e.g. while a clear is inactive. Release (recovery) checks never allow simultaneous clock/data changes.
tools.usage: + SETUP_HOLD: CLOCK LH|HL=<node> DATA(<n>)=<node>* [SETUPTIME=<t> | SETUPTIME_LO=<t> SETUPTIME_HI=<t>] [HOLDTIME=<t> | HOLDTIME_LO/HI=<t>] [RELEASETIME=<t> | RELEASETIME_LH/HL=<t>] [WHEN {<bool>}] [MESSAGE="<text>"] [ERRORLIMIT=<n>] [AFFECTS_ALL|AFFECTS_NONE|AFFECTS(<n>)=<outputs>]

parameters.name: CLOCK <edge>=<node>
parameters.description: Reference edge; LH rising, HL falling.

parameters.name: DATA(n)
parameters.description: Nodes that must be stable around the clock edge.

parameters.name: AFFECTS
parameters.description: PINDLY only: which outputs become X/hazard after a violation.

tools.example: + SETUP_HOLD: CLOCK LH=CLK DATA(2)=D0 D1 SETUPTIME=10ns HOLDTIME=2ns WHEN {PRE=='1' & CLR=='1'} MESSAGE="74LS74 D setup/hold"
tools.notes: If CLOCK or DATA is X at check time nothing is reported. Violations are reported at the non-asserting edge, so they may appear out of order in the .out file.

tools.name: WIDTH: / FREQ: / GENERAL: constraint sections
tools.description: Remaining constraint checkers: WIDTH reports pulses on a node narrower than MIN_LOW/MIN_HIGH; FREQ reports a node whose frequency is below MINFREQ or above MAXFREQ; GENERAL evaluates a Boolean expression of the inputs (optionally with a LIMIT time window) and reports when it is true. All accept WHEN, MESSAGE and ERRORLIMIT like SETUP_HOLD.
tools.usage:
+ WIDTH: NODE=<node> [MIN_LOW=<t>] [MIN_HIGH=<t>] [WHEN {..}] [MESSAGE=".."] [ERRORLIMIT=<n>]
+ FREQ: NODE=<node> [MINFREQ=<f>] [MAXFREQ=<f>] [WHEN {..}] [MESSAGE=".."]
+ GENERAL: [WHEN {<bool>}] [LIMIT=<t>] [MESSAGE=".."] [ERRORLIMIT=<n>] [AFFECTS ...]

parameters.name: MIN_LOW / MIN_HIGH
parameters.description: Minimum low/high pulse width.

parameters.name: MINFREQ / MAXFREQ
parameters.description: Allowed frequency window.

tools.example:
+ WIDTH: NODE=CLRBAR MIN_LOW=25ns MESSAGE="clear pulse too short"
+ FREQ: NODE=CLK MAXFREQ=33MEG
+ GENERAL: WHEN {(PRE=='0') & (CLR=='0')} MESSAGE="preset and clear both active"

tools.name: STIM (digital stimulus generator)
tools.description: Generates digital waveforms on one or more nodes from a script of <time> <value> commands. (<width>,<format array>) sets the number of signals and how each digit of a value is interpreted (1 = binary, 3 = octal, 4 = hex digit). TIMESTEP defines the clock-cycle unit for times written with a C suffix; times may be absolute or relative (+5ns). The script supports labels, GOTO loops, INCR/DECR and REPEAT blocks.
tools.usage:
U<name> STIM(<width>,<format array>) <pwr> <gnd> <node>* <UIO model> [STIMULUS=<name>] [IO_LEVEL=..] [TIMESTEP=<stepsize>]
+ <time> <value>
+ LABEL=<label>
+ <time> GOTO <label> <n> TIMES | UNTIL GT|GE|LT|LE <value>
+ <time> INCR BY <value> | DECR BY <value>
+ REPEAT FOREVER | REPEAT <n> TIMES ... ENDREPEAT
+ FILE=<file name>

parameters.name: <format array>
parameters.description: Digits summing to <width>, each 1, 3 or 4.

parameters.name: <value>
parameters.description: Per-node states 0 1 R F X Z, or hex/octal digits per the format.

parameters.name: TIMESTEP
parameters.description: Seconds per clock cycle for C-suffixed times.

tools.example:
UCLK STIM(1,1) $G_DPWR $G_DGND CLK IO_STM TIMESTEP=10ns
+ 0c 0
+ LABEL=LOOP
+ +1c 1
+ +1c 0
+ +0c GOTO LOOP -1 TIMES
UBUS STIM(4,4) $G_DPWR $G_DGND A3 A2 A1 A0 IO_STM
+ 0ns 0
+ 50ns INCR BY 1
+ 100ns GOTO LOOP UNTIL GE F
tools.notes: IO_STM from dig_io.lib is the standard stimulus I/O model. Capture parts STIM1/STIM4/STIM8/STIM16 and DIGCLOCK/DIGSTIM expose this; the Stimulus Editor writes .STIMULUS ... STIM definitions.

tools.name: FSTIM (file stimulus device)
tools.description: Drives digital nodes from a stimulus file whose header names signals and whose body lists time/state rows (the same format .VECTOR writes), so one simulation's results, a logic-simulator dump or a hand-written table can stimulate a circuit. SIGNAMES maps file columns to nodes when the names differ.
tools.usage: U<name> FSTIM(<# outputs>) <pwr> <gnd> <node>* <UIO model> FILE=<stimulus file name> [IO_LEVEL=..] [SIGNAMES=<file signal name>*]

parameters.name: FILE
parameters.description: Required; quoted string or |text expression|.

parameters.name: SIGNAMES
parameters.description: Column names positionally matched to the node list.

tools.example:
U1 FSTIM(1) $G_DPWR $G_DGND IN1 IO_STM FILE=DIG1.STM
U2 FSTIM(4) $G_DPWR $G_DGND ADDR3 ADDR2 ADDR1 ADDR0 IO_STM FILE=DIG_2.STM SIGNAMES=AD3 AD2 AD1 AD0
tools.notes: Capture part FILESTIM1/4/8/16/32 wraps it; the profile's Configuration Files > Stimulus category lists the .stm files.

tools.name: Timing model parameter naming (TP, TSU, TH, TW, TSW with MN/TY/MX)
tools.description: Every timing-model parameter is built from a kind prefix (TP propagation delay, TSU setup, TH hold, TW pulse width, TSW switching), a path/edge description and a MN/TY/MX suffix: TPLHTY is the typical low-to-high gate delay, TSUDCLKMN the minimum data-to-clock setup of a flip-flop, TWCLKHMX the maximum clock-high width. Missing propagation delays are extrapolated with DIGMNTYSCALE/DIGTYMXSCALE; missing constraints default to 0 (min), the typical (max) or the average (typ).
tools.usage: .MODEL <name> <UGATE|UTGATE|UEFF|UGFF|UDLY|UPLD|UROM|URAM|UADC|UDAC|UBTG>(<param>MN=.. <param>TY=.. <param>MX=.. ...)

parameters.name: UGATE
parameters.description: TPLHMN/TY/MX, TPHLMN/TY/MX.

parameters.name: UTGATE
parameters.description: adds TPZH*, TPZL*, TPHZ*, TPLZ*.

parameters.name: UEFF
parameters.description: TPCLKQLH*, TPCLKQHL*, TPPCQLH*, TPPCQHL*, TSUDCLK*, THDCLK*, TSUPCCLKH*, TWPCL*, TWCLKL*, TWCLKH*, TSUCECLK*, THCECLK*.

parameters.name: UGFF
parameters.description: TPDQ*, TPGQ*, TPPCQ*, TSUDG*, THDG*, TWG*, TWPC*.

tools.example:
.MODEL D_74LS00 UGATE(TPLHMN=3ns TPLHTY=9ns TPLHMX=15ns TPHLMN=3ns TPHLTY=10ns TPHLMX=15ns)
.MODEL T_JKFF UEFF(TPCLKQLHTY=20ns TPCLKQHLTY=25ns TSUDCLKMN=20ns THDCLKMN=0 TWCLKHMN=25ns)

tools.name: UIO model (digital I/O model parameters)
tools.description: Describes a device family's loading and driving: INLD/OUTLD input/output load capacitance, DRVH/DRVL output resistances (strength), DRVZ high-impedance leakage, INR input leakage, TSTOREMN minimum storage time for charge-storage nets, TPWRT pulse-width rejection threshold, TSWLHn/TSWHLn switching-time corrections for each DtoA level, DIGPOWER (power subcircuit, default DIGIFPWR) and the names of AtoD1-4 and DtoA1-4 interface subcircuits. One UIO model serves a whole family (IO_LS, IO_LS_OC, IO_LS_ST, IO_LS_OC_ST for 74LS).
tools.usage: .MODEL <name> UIO(INLD=<F> OUTLD=<F> DRVH=<ohm> DRVL=<ohm> DRVZ=<ohm> INR=<ohm> TSTOREMN=<s> TPWRT=<s> TSWLH1=<s> TSWHL1=<s> ... DIGPOWER="<subckt>" AtoD1="<subckt>" DtoA1="<subckt>" ... AtoD4 DtoA4)

parameters.name: DRVH / DRVL
parameters.description: Output high/low resistance, default 50 ohm; bounded by DIGDRVF/DIGDRVZ.

parameters.name: INLD / OUTLD
parameters.description: Load capacitances that add to propagation delay, default 0.

parameters.name: AtoDn / DtoAn
parameters.description: Interface subcircuits inserted for IO_LEVEL n; default AtoDDefault/DtoADefault.

parameters.name: TSTOREMN
parameters.description: Minimum charge-storage time, default 1 ms.

tools.example: .MODEL IO_STD UIO(DRVH=96.4 DRVL=104 AtoD1="AtoD_STD" AtoD2="AtoD_STD_NX" AtoD3="AtoD_STD" AtoD4="AtoD_STD_NX" DtoA1="DtoA_STD" DtoA2="DtoA_STD" DtoA3="DtoA_STD" DtoA4="DtoA_STD" TSWHL1=1.373ns TSWLH1=3.382ns DIGPOWER="DIGIFPWR")
tools.notes: Stimulus devices have no inputs, so INLD and AtoDn are ignored for them. Copy an existing family model from dig_io.lib when creating a new one.

tools.name: IO_STD / IO_LS / IO_HC / IO_AC / IO_ECL / IO_4000 / IO_STM (library I/O models)
tools.description: The I/O models shipped in dig_io.lib and used by the digital part libraries: IO_STD (standard TTL), IO_LS, IO_ALS, IO_AS, IO_F, IO_HC, IO_HCT, IO_AC, IO_ACT, IO_4000 (CD4000 CMOS), IO_ECL, each with _OC (open collector) and _ST (Schmitt) variants, plus IO_STM for stimulus generators and IO_BTG for transfer gates. Selecting the right family model gives correct thresholds, loading and interface subcircuits at analog boundaries.
tools.usage: U<name> <primitive> ... <timing model> IO_<family>[_OC][_ST]

parameters.name: _OC
parameters.description: Open-collector output (DRVH very high).

parameters.name: _ST
parameters.description: Schmitt-trigger input thresholds in the AtoD subcircuits.

tools.example:
U1 NAND(2) $G_DPWR $G_DGND A B Y D_74HC00 IO_HC
UCLK STIM(1,1) $G_DPWR $G_DGND CLK IO_STM 0s 0 +50ns 1 +50ns 0

tools.name: AtoD / DtoA interface subcircuits and DIGIFPWR
tools.description: When a node connects both analog and digital devices PSpice inserts an interface subcircuit named in the I/O model: AtoD_<family> (an O device with a DOUTPUT model) or DtoA_<family> (an N device with a DINPUT model), powered by the DIGIFPWR power subcircuit that creates the $G_DPWR/$G_DGND supplies (5 V by default). Levels 1/2 use full analog models; levels 3/4 (_D variants) keep the net digital where possible for speed.
tools.usage: IO_LEVEL=1..4 on the U device, or .OPTIONS DIGIOLVL; interface names come from AtoDn/DtoAn in the UIO model; power from DIGPOWER="DIGIFPWR"

parameters.name: AtoD_STD / DtoA_STD
parameters.description: TTL interfaces; _HC, _LS, _AC, _4000, _ECL variants per family.

parameters.name: DIGIFPWR
parameters.description: Subcircuit providing the digital supply; override VOLTAGE via its parameter or your own DIGPOWER subcircuit.

tools.example:
* dig_io.lib excerpt
.subckt DtoA_STD D A DPWR DGND params: DRVL=0 DRVH=0 CAPACITANCE=0
N1 A DGND DPWR DIN_STD DGTLNET=D IO_STD
C1 A DGND {CAPACITANCE+0.1pF}
.ends
tools.notes: The interface nodes appear in Probe as <node>$AtoD / <node>$DtoA. Use the Options > Gate-level Simulation 'Default I/O level' to choose globally.

tools.name: $G_DPWR / $G_DGND / $D_HI / $D_LO (digital global nodes)
tools.description: Global nets used throughout the digital libraries: $G_DPWR and $G_DGND are the digital power and ground nodes (created by DIGIFPWR at 5 V), passed as OPTIONAL: subcircuit nodes so every 74xx part shares them; $D_HI and $D_LO are constant logic-1 and logic-0 nodes for tying off unused inputs. Capture provides the HI, LO, DIGPWR and DIGGND symbols for the same purpose.
tools.usage:
X1 A B Y 74LS00            ; uses $G_DPWR/$G_DGND by default
X2 A B Y MYPWR MYGND 74LS00 ; explicit supplies
tools.example: U1 DFF(1) $G_DPWR $G_DGND $D_HI $D_HI CLK D Q QB T_DFF IO_STD
tools.notes: Mixing 3.3 V CMOS and 5 V TTL families needs separate DIGPOWER subcircuits with their own supply nodes.

tools.name: Digital worst-case timing (MNTYMXDLY=4 / DIGMNTYMX=4)
tools.description: Min/max mode simulates each delay as an ambiguity region between its minimum and maximum values instead of a single typical value, propagating rising/falling ambiguity through the logic. Hazards are reported when ambiguities converge to produce a glitch (AMBIGUITY CONVERGENCE), accumulate until edges overlap (CUMULATIVE AMBIGUITY), or a pulse narrower than the delay is suppressed (SUPPRESSED GLITCH); those reaching storage or .EXTERNAL nets become PERSISTENT HAZARDs.
tools.usage:
.OPTIONS DIGMNTYMX=4        ; whole design
U1 NAND(2) ... MNTYMXDLY=4   ; one device

parameters.name: Hazard messages
parameters.description: AMBIGUITY CONVERGENCE, CUMULATIVE AMBIGUITY, SUPPRESSED GLITCH, NET-STATE CONFLICT, DIGITAL INPUT VOLTAGE, PERSISTENT HAZARD, ZERO-DELAY-OSCILLATION.

tools.example:
.OPTIONS DIGMNTYMX=4 DIGERRLIMIT=100
.EXTERNAL OUTPUT DATA_OUT
* run TRAN and read the Hazards section of the .out file
tools.notes: Timing-violation and hazard messages can be filtered/suppressed with NOOUTMSG/NOPRBMSG and are shown in Probe as markers on the offending traces. A node toggling more than 50 times in one digital time step is flagged as ZERO-DELAY-OSCILLATION and the run is cancelled.

tools.name: Timing violation messages (SETUP, HOLD, RELEASE, WIDTH, FREQUENCY, GENERAL)
tools.description: The categories of digital condition messages written to the .out file and Probe data: SETUP/HOLD (data not stable before/after the clock edge), RELEASE (control released too close to the clock), WIDTH (pulse too narrow), FREQUENCY (period too long/short) and GENERAL (a user Boolean became true). They originate from CONSTRAINT/PINDLY sections and can be capped with DIGERRDEFAULT/DIGERRLIMIT.
tools.usage: View > Output File (search for 'WARNING' / 'VIOLATION') or Probe: View > Simulation Messages
tools.example:
* .out excerpt
**** DIGITAL TIMING VIOLATIONS
SETUP VIOLATION at 250.0ns on U3 (D_74LS74): DATA=D changed 3.5ns before CLK LH; SETUPTIME=20ns
tools.notes: Probe's Simulation Message Summary dialog lists them with a Plot button that opens the involved traces at the violation time.

tools.name: Digital stimulus file format (.stm / .vec)
tools.description: ASCII table read by FSTIM and written by .VECTOR: an optional TIMESCALE line, a header naming the signals (with radix groupings), then rows of <time> <state values>. Times are absolute unless prefixed with +, and multi-bit columns use hex/octal per the header. Because both ends use the same format, digital results can be chained between simulations or exchanged with external logic simulators.
tools.usage:
* header
TIMESCALE=1ns
STATE  CLK  DATA
0      0    0
+10    1    1
+10    0    1

parameters.name: TIMESCALE
parameters.description: Multiplier applied to the time column.

parameters.name: +<t>
parameters.description: Time relative to the previous row.

tools.example: U1 FSTIM(2) $G_DPWR $G_DGND CLK DATA IO_STM FILE="pattern.stm" SIGNAMES=CLK DATA

tools.name: STIM1 / STIM4 / STIM8 / STIM16, DIGCLOCK, DIGSTIM, FILESTIM (Capture stimulus parts)
tools.description: Schematic front ends for the digital stimulus primitives in source.olb/sourcstm.olb: STIM1/4/8/16 hold the STIM command script in COMMAND1..COMMAND16 properties (with TIMESTEP, FORMAT, IO_LEVEL); DIGCLOCK generates a clock from ONTIME/OFFTIME/DELAY/STARTVAL/OPPVAL; DIGSTIM references a Stimulus Editor definition via STIMULUS; FILESTIM1..32 wrap FSTIM with FILENAME and SIGNAME properties.
tools.usage: Place > PSpice Component > Digital > (stimulus) or Place > Part > sourcstm.olb / source.olb

parameters.name: COMMANDn
parameters.description: STIM script lines, e.g. 0s 0, +10ns 1, +10ns GOTO ...

parameters.name: ONTIME / OFFTIME
parameters.description: DIGCLOCK high and low durations.

tools.example:
1. Place DIGCLOCK, set ONTIME=50ns OFFTIME=50ns.
2. Place STIM4 on a 4-bit bus, set FORMAT=4, COMMAND1=0ns 0, COMMAND2=+100ns INCR BY 1, COMMAND3=+100ns GOTO 2 -1 TIMES.
3. Run transient and view D(BUS) in Probe.

tools.name: Digital Probe traces: D(), bus display and digital plot
tools.description: Digital nodes appear in Probe as D(node) traces drawn in the separate digital pane with states 0, 1, X (hatched), Z (dashed) and R/F transitions; busses can be grouped and shown in hex/octal/binary/decimal by wrapping the bits in braces {A3 A2 A1 A0}, and the Plot > Digital Size command sets the pane height. Time-cursor readout shows the state at the cursor.
tools.usage: Trace > Add Trace > D(<node>)   |   {D(A3) D(A2) D(A1) D(A0);h}   (h hex, o octal, d decimal, b binary)

parameters.name: {bits;radix}
parameters.description: Bus grouping with optional radix suffix.

tools.example: Trace > Add Trace: D(CLK) D(Q) {D(BUS3) D(BUS2) D(BUS1) D(BUS0);h}
tools.notes: Digital and analog traces can share the X axis; markers on digital nets in Capture (PSpice > Markers > Voltage Level) plot D() automatically. Use Plot > Add Plot to Window to separate busses.

tools.name: Gate-level simulation options (profile Options tab)
tools.description: The Simulation Settings > Options > Gate-level Simulation category maps to the DIG* options: Timing Mode (Minimum/Typical/Maximum/Worst-case = DIGMNTYMX), 'Suppress simulation error messages in waveform data file' (NOPRBMSG), 'Initialize all flip-flops to' (DIGINITSTATE 0/1/X) and 'Default I/O level for A/D interfaces' (DIGIOLVL 1-4). Advanced options expose DIGMNTYSCALE, DIGTYMXSCALE, DIGDRVF, DIGDRVZ, DIGOVRDRV, DIGERRDEFAULT, DIGERRLIMIT and DIGFREQ.
tools.usage: PSpice > Edit Simulation Profile > Options > Category: Gate-level Simulation

parameters.name: Timing Mode
parameters.description: Minimum / Typical / Maximum / Worst-case (min/max).

parameters.name: Initialize all flip-flops to
parameters.description: 0, 1 or X.

parameters.name: Default I/O level
parameters.description: 1 (analog interfaces) to 4.

tools.example:
1. Open the profile, Options tab, select Gate-level Simulation.
2. Set Timing Mode = Worst-case (min/max) and Initialize flip-flops = 0.
3. Run; inspect the Hazard messages via View > Simulation Messages in Probe.
